{"status":"abandon","summary":"I implemented the plan and it builds, but it gives no speedup, so I'm abandoning it. Changes: (1) PushInFilter wraps IN-lists of at most 16 values with a numeric/varchar physical type in a SelectivityOptionalFilter (threshold 0.5, 30 check vectors) instead of a plain OptionalFilter. (2) ColumnSegment::FilterSelection gets a typed IN_FILTER case. (3) TableFilterState::Initialize gets IN_FILTER support (empty state). (4) ConstantFun::FiltersNullValues gets IN_FILTER support (filters NULLs). Effect in q02.m0: the supplier TABLE_SCAN now emits 20,051 rows instead of about 96k, but its cumulative time stays at 0.07s. Bench: q02 52.1ms best vs 53.0ms mine (+1.8%, noise). Root cause: the issue assumed the unfiltered scan decompresses every FSST string. It doesn't. FSSTStorage::StringScan emits lazy FSST_VECTORs, while the filtered path (FSSTStorage::Select) decompresses eagerly. Direct check on the 100k-row table, s_name and s_phone only: unfiltered scan 0.02s, scan with a strict 20%-selective filter (s_nationkey<5) 0.03s. Adding all 7 columns with a strict selective filter still gives 0.06s. So early row filtering does not make this scan cheaper.","generality":"The change would let any equality hash join whose build side has a small, non-dense key set filter probe-table rows during the scan. It only saves work when the skipped columns are eagerly decoded or copied (uncompressed or bitpacked payloads). For FSST string payloads it saves nothing, and it can cost more, because the Select path decodes eagerly where a full scan would defer.","notes":"- Dead end: filtering rows early to save string decompression does not work for FSST columns. A full scan already emits lazy FSST vectors; the Select path decompresses eagerly. Check compression with pragma_storage_info and compare filtered vs unfiltered scan time with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before proposing ideas like this.
- The supplier scan cost (about 0.06s cumulative for 100k rows, 7 columns, one row group) is not proportional to rows selected. Something per-vector or per-morsel probably dominates. One candidate: FSST StartScan delta-decodes offsets from the segment start whenever a new morsel begins mid-segment (last_known_row resets on a fresh scan state), and sub-row-group morsels (commit E0001) make that happen more often. Another: the 12 uncompressed string segments. Worth profiling.
- Side finding: RowGroup::CheckZonemap marks top-level OPTIONAL_FILTERs as always-true. A SelectivityOptionalFilter only runs on rows when it sits inside a CONJUNCTION_AND, which happens here because min/max filters are pushed alongside.
- The IN_FILTER FilterSelection, Initialize and FiltersNullValues cases are correct and could be reused if row-level IN filtering is wanted elsewhere. BOOL was left out (std::vector<bool> doesn't compile in the typed loop, and a two-value bool list is always dense anyway)."}

structured_output.summary: I implemented the plan and it builds, but it gives no speedup, so I'm abandoning it. Changes: (1) PushInFilter wraps IN-lists of at most 16 values with a numeric/varchar physical type in a SelectivityOptionalFilter (threshold 0.5, 30 check vectors) instead of a plain OptionalFilter. (2) ColumnSegment::FilterSelection gets a typed IN_FILTER case. (3) TableFilterState::Initialize gets IN_FILTER support (empty state). (4) ConstantFun::FiltersNullValues gets IN_FILTER support (filters NULLs). Effect in q02.m0: the supplier TABLE_SCAN now emits 20,051 rows instead of about 96k, but its cumulative time stays at 0.07s. Bench: q02 52.1ms best vs 53.0ms mine (+1.8%, noise). Root cause: the issue assumed the unfiltered scan decompresses every FSST string. It doesn't. FSSTStorage::StringScan emits lazy FSST_VECTORs, while the filtered path (FSSTStorage::Select) decompresses eagerly. Direct check on the 100k-row table, s_name and s_phone only: unfiltered scan 0.02s, scan with a strict 20%-selective filter (s_nationkey<5) 0.03s. Adding all 7 columns with a strict selective filter still gives 0.06s. So early row filtering does not make this scan cheaper.
structured_output.generality: The change would let any equality hash join whose build side has a small, non-dense key set filter probe-table rows during the scan. It only saves work when the skipped columns are eagerly decoded or copied (uncompressed or bitpacked payloads). For FSST string payloads it saves nothing, and it can cost more, because the Select path decodes eagerly where a full scan would defer.
structured_output.notes:
- Dead end: filtering rows early to save string decompression does not work for FSST columns. A full scan already emits lazy FSST vectors; the Select path decompresses eagerly. Check compression with pragma_storage_info and compare filtered vs unfiltered scan time with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before proposing ideas like this.
- The supplier scan cost (about 0.06s cumulative for 100k rows, 7 columns, one row group) is not proportional to rows selected. Something per-vector or per-morsel probably dominates. One candidate: FSST StartScan delta-decodes offsets from the segment start whenever a new morsel begins mid-segment (last_known_row resets on a fresh scan state), and sub-row-group morsels (commit E0001) make that happen more often. Another: the 12 uncompressed string segments. Worth profiling.
- Side finding: RowGroup::CheckZonemap marks top-level OPTIONAL_FILTERs as always-true. A SelectivityOptionalFilter only runs on rows when it sits inside a CONJUNCTION_AND, which happens here because min/max filters are pushed alongside.
- The IN_FILTER FilterSelection, Initialize and FiltersNullValues cases are correct and could be reused if row-level IN filtering is wanted elsewhere. BOOL was left out (std::vector<bool> doesn't compile in the typed loop, and a two-value bool list is always dense anyway).
